title: Generic React Best Practices
note: Load `tailwind-design-system` only when implementing or reviewing code inside `shared/ui`, where advanced styling and design-system patterns belong. Composing shared UI primitives and using basic layout classes in domain code do not require that skill. This catalog owns architecture, composition, client-side performance and custom ESLint requirements, and takes precedence over conflicting companion guidance.
abstract: Opinionated React/TypeScript guidelines for any front-end app (React 19, TanStack Query v5, Jotai, Yup, react-i18next, Jest + React Testing Library), designed for AI agents and LLMs. The catalog covers domain-first architecture and import boundaries, API hooks and server state, query keys and cache invalidation, domain types, Yup schemas, UI composition and accessibility, Jotai client state, helpers, i18n, testing, code quality and client-side performance. Each rule includes a rationale and incorrect vs. correct examples using generic business vocabulary. The catalog also owns capability mapping, feature hierarchy, shared UI styling and accessibility boundaries, semantic colors, nested-children composition, component complexity review and public API maintenance.
